subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a public synchronous plugin/API config-write veto hook, and what exact ordering, metadata, timeout, recursion, and failure semantics should it use?
rationale: This would let plugin code block persisted core config writes, which is useful for external validators but changes a sensitive runtime/plugin API boundary that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Define guarded config pre-apply hook
options.body: Add a narrow typed hook with current config, pending config, action, raw payload or patch, base hash, actor metadata, changed paths, and a typed reject result, with regression tests proving rejection leaves disk and runtime state unchanged.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight framework
options.body: Defer this issue to a unified preflight/validation design so config writes, startup checks, and plugin validation share one maintainer-approved security model.

options.title: Keep built-in validation only
options.body: Reject a plugin veto API for now and rely on built-in validation, SecretRef preflight, the agent-tool allowlist, doctor, and voluntary external tools such as config-guard.

recommendation.title: Define guarded config pre-apply hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow typed hook with current config, pending config, action, raw payload or patch, base hash, actor metadata, changed paths, and a typed reject result, with regression tests proving rejection leaves disk and runtime state unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: They already provided the strongest product-routing review on this issue and have merged or recently touched the central config/gateway surfaces.
